title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
events_chronological: In 1918 the blind clockmaker Mr. Gateau builds a station clock that runs backwards, in memory of the son he lost in the war.
On the night the war ends, Thomas Button's wife dies in childbirth and he abandons the baby - an infant with the body of an old man - on the steps of a nursing home.
Queenie, who runs the home, takes Benjamin in and raises him among the elderly residents.
Benjamin, apparently in his eighties, gets out of his wheelchair and walks.
Benjamin meets six-year-old Daisy, the granddaughter of a resident, and the two become inseparable.
Benjamin takes work on Captain Mike's tugboat and leaves New Orleans for the first time.
Wintering in Murmansk, Benjamin has an affair with Elizabeth Abbott, the wife of a British trade official.
The tug is drafted into the war and Captain Mike and most of the crew are killed ramming a German submarine.
Benjamin comes home, and Thomas Button reveals himself as his father and leaves him the button factory.
Daisy, now a dancer in New York, visits, and Benjamin turns her down as too young for him.
Daisy's leg is shattered by a car in Paris and she refuses Benjamin's help.
Her dancing over, Daisy comes back to New Orleans, and she and Benjamin finally meet in the middle of their lives.
Queenie dies, and Benjamin and Daisy sell up and live together on a boat and then in a house of their own.
Their daughter Caroline is born, and Benjamin, visibly younger every year, decides she cannot have a father who will become her brother.
Benjamin signs everything over to Daisy and leaves.
Daisy marries again and raises Caroline, while Benjamin travels the world alone and sends postcards.
Benjamin comes back once, in his twenties, and spends a night with Daisy before leaving again.
In the 1980s Daisy is called to collect a boy found in a derelict building with Benjamin's diary, and cares for him as he forgets everything.
Benjamin dies in Daisy's arms as an infant.
In 2005, with Hurricane Katrina coming, Caroline finishes reading the diary to her dying mother and learns who her father was, while the backwards clock sits in a flooding storage room.
syuzhet_notes: This is a frame narrative rather than a shuffled one: told-order bullet 1 is the 2005 hospital room, and everything after it is the contents of Benjamin's diary, read aloud in chronological order. The frame is not confined to the opening - it interrupts the diary repeatedly across the runtime, so the present-day material recurs where a single ordering can place it only once. What runs backwards in this film is the protagonist's body, not the telling.
fabula_notes: Benjamin ages in reverse, so his apparent age and his actual age move in opposite directions throughout; the ordering here follows chronological time rather than how old he looks. The years covered by the postcards are a montage, and Caroline's discovery of her parentage belongs to the frame's own present rather than to the diary.
